rows.label: Concept
rows.text: A series LCR circuit combines resistance, inductance, and capacitance. It demonstrates resonance when inductive and capacitive reactances cancel, leading to minimum impedance and maximum current.

rows.label: Formula
rows.text:
Impedance Z = √(R² + (X_L - X_C)²)
Resonance frequency f_r = 1 / (2π√LC)
Phase angle φ = tan⁻¹((X_L - X_C) / R)

rows.label: Conditions
rows.text: ❌ Believing resonance occurs at all frequencies ✅ Resonance occurs only at a specific frequency (f_r = 1 / (2π√LC)) where inductive reactance equals capacitive reactance (X_L = X_C).  ·  ❌ Misinterpreting phase angle as constant ✅ The phase angle φ (where tan φ = (X_L - X_C) / R) depends on the frequency of the AC source; it is zero at resonance.

rows.label: Special cases
rows.text: Note 1: Resonance occurs when X_L = X_C.  ·  Note 2: At resonance, current is in phase with voltage (φ=0).

rows.label: Solved
rows.text: Calculating impedance and phase angle  ·  Finding resonance frequency

rows.label: Limitation
rows.text: ❌ Assuming voltage across L and C is zero at resonance ✅ While the net voltage across the L-C combination is zero (because they are 180° out of phase), individual voltages across L and C can be non-zero and large.

rows.label: Study notes
rows.text: **LCR Series Circuit:** An AC circuit containing a resistor (R), inductor (L), and capacitor (C) connected in series.  ·  The behavior is determined by the combination of resistance and reactance (inductive and capacitive).  ·  It exhibits resonance when the net reactance is zero.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: Concept 5: Q-Factor  ·  Current I = V / Z  ·  Quality Factor Q = (1/R)√(L/C)
